item.description:

Leonardo’s UK Loss Shows the Cost of Renting Hotels

Rising wages and payroll taxes are squeezing Leonardo Hotels' UK business, but the bigger problem is the rent on its hotels, according to accounts filed with Companies House, the UK company register.

On paper, the drop is steep. The hotel chain swung to a £55.6 million ($74 million) pre-tax loss in 2025 from a £50.1 million ($67 million) profit. But the 2024 profit included an £89.8 million ($119 million) one-off gain from revaluing its leases. Without it, 2024 would have shown a loss of about £40 million ($53 million), so the loss widened by about £16 million ($21 million) rather than appearing from nowhere.

The filing shows revenue at Leonardo Hotel Management (UK) Ltd was steady, rising 1.3% to £350.1 million ($466 million), with no new hotels opened. Gross profit fell 12% to £37.6 million ($50 million), and the gross margin slipped to 10.7% from 12.4%. Staff costs rose 6% to £102.5 million ($136 million), and employer social security costs rose 34%.

Why Global Hotel Alliance Is Turning to Saudi Arabia Despite Riyadh’s Slump

Global Hotel Alliance, a Dubai-headquartered network of independent hotel brands, plans to grow in Saudi Arabia rather than add many more hotels in the UAE, CEO Christopher Hartley told Skift.

GHA’s network covers 1,000 hotels and over 60 brands across 100 countries.

“We don’t need to add another 30 or 40 hotels just for the sake of it,” he said of the UAE, where GHA now has about 70 hotels, including properties from home-grown operator Rotana, and from Minor International, Kempinski, Nikki Beach, Cheval Collection and JA Resorts.

Global Hotel Alliance CEO Chris Hartley speaking at Skift Asia Forum in Delhi in March 2025.

The shift follows a hard year in its home market. The U.S.-Iran war cut GHA’s loyalty revenue in the UAE by 28% on a like-for-like basis to $134 million through October, Hartley said. Agoda’s COO on AI Booking: ‘Nobody Knows’ the Business Model Yet

AI booking is "definitely disruptive to our industry," Agoda's chief operating officer Ittai Chorev said at a media roundtable in Bangkok on Thursday. But "in terms of how the business model or commercials will look, nobody knows." For now, he said, that works in Agoda's favor: the AI platforms are "in the growth stage, so everything is free, which is great for us."

The Booking Holdings-owned online travel agency was one of the first travel partners in Asia to integrate with Meta's Muse, an AI agent that can search and book on a user's behalf, and it works with OpenAI and Microsoft on its internal tools.

How well Agoda uses AI matters beyond its own app. Booking Holdings is building its new B2B unit mainly on Agoda's partner technology, Skift reported in August, so Agoda's AI work will shape more of the group's business.

Norse Atlantic Collapses as Norwegian Arm Files for Bankruptcy

Norse Atlantic Airways has canceled all flights and discontinued ticket sales after its Norwegian operating subsidiary said it is filing for bankruptcy.

The collapse comes a day after the low-cost, long-haul carrier suspended flights and two days after it described its financial situation as “critical.”

In a stock exchange filing on Friday, Norse confirmed that the board of its Norwegian operating subsidiary, Norse Atlantic Airways AS, had concluded there was no longer a basis for continued operations. The board resolved to file a bankruptcy petition with a local court, which will appoint a trustee to oversee the process.

The filing does not extend to the listed parent company, Norse Atlantic ASA, or its UK operating subsidiary. Norse said efforts are continuing to find a solution that would allow the remaining parts of the business to continue operating.

item.title: What’s in my bag: The Points Guy, Brian Kelly’s travel essentials
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Personal travel gear with some useful vocabulary.

Welcome to “What’s in My Bag,” a new series where TPG staffers open their carry-ons, personal items and dopp kits to share the travel essentials they never leave home without.

Meet the traveler: Brian Kelly, founder of The Points Guy

- Home airport: Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) or John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK)

- Bag of choice: Lululemon New Crew Backpack Large 30L, $128

- Travel style: Carry-on if traveling solo, check a bag if I’m with my kids

- Next trip: The Philippines

What’s in my bag

As a travel expert who’s constantly on the go, I will say some of my favorite things that you’ll find in my bag revolve around staying organized and being comfortable — I always know where my essentials are. At this stage of my life, I’m willing to splurge a bit on handcrafted or well-made products that last. Quality is nonnegotiable.

Prada Re-Nylon and Saffiano leather travel pouch

This travel pouch is so chic, but definitely a splurge. It’s made with Saffiano leather and Re-Nylon, an innovative fabric that’s produced from recycled plastic recovered from the ocean. You can find it at Saks Fifth Avenue. I love it for keeping everything I might need on the go organized — with two top zipper pockets and one each on the front and back, I never run out of room.

Buy: Prada Re-Nylon and Saffiano leather travel pouch, $1,120

Bose QuietComfort Ultra headphones

These Bose noise-canceling headphones are comfortable and seamlessly connect via Bluetooth. Plus, they are stylish and have great sound quality. The surround sound is awesome.

Buy: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones, from $349 (normally $449)

Rode wireless microphones

As a content creator, I needed a good lav microphone with an iPhone receiver for when I’m out and about. The Rode wireless mic is super easy to use, holds a charge all day and slips right into my travel pouch.

Buy: Rode ultra-compact wireless microphone system with USB-C connector, $89 (normally $99)

Healthy snacks

My go-to quick snack is Quest protein peanut butter cups — indulgent yet packed with protein. I keep Grüns gummies in my bag for a healthy mix of essential vitamins and prebiotics. They keep me feeling energized and are more than just a multivitamin — they’re made with whole fruits and veggies too.

Buy: Grüns sugar-free gummies (pack of 28), $73.32; Quest protein peanut butter cups (pack of 12), $28.49

Aspinal of London wallet

I firmly believe in investing in pieces that will last, and this handcrafted leather wallet from Aspinal of London is no exception. It holds up to eight cards and can be personalized with your initials.

Buy: Aspinal of London 8-card billfold wallet in black woven leather, $180 (normally $355)

Extra iPhone

I have a second phone for travel that’s connected to the T-Mobile network as a backup, and, depending on your service plan, T-Mobile also offers free Wi-Fi on U.S. airlines. I keep my main phone on Verizon, but you never want to be stuck without a phone when abroad.

Buy: iPhone 18 Pro, from $1,199

Wimbledon hat

I’m a big tennis fan, whether it’s traveling for a match or catching the U.S. Open when it's in New York. This easy-to-adjust hat is perfect to keep in my bag, so I always have one on me for sun protection.

Buy: Wimbledon Mono-tone Herringbone Cap, $64

Tom Ford Snowdon sunglasses

Fashionable sun protection is a no-brainer. I love these Tom Ford sunglasses in black.

Buy: Tom Ford Snowdon sunglasses, $284 (normally $316)

Insignia international converter and plug adapters

This small device is super versatile — not only does it convert 220–240V AC input to 120V AC output, but it also includes five plug adapters so I can use it in nearly every country in the world.

Buy: Insignia international converter and plug adapters, $17.49 (normally $29.99)

UGreen power bank

This portable power bank gives me peace of mind knowing I can charge my phone on the go. Small and lightweight, it fits on the back of my iPhone without covering the camera and fits easily into my pocket or travel pouch.

Buy: UGreen 10000mAh 22.5W compact power bank, $19.99 (normally $29.99)

Notebook for travel journaling

I never know when an idea will strike, or when I need to jot down a few meeting notes on the go. The Moleskine XL leather-bound hardcover notebook feels luxurious and has large pages that make writing easier.

Buy: Moleskine classic hardcover XL notebook, $24.75

Supergoop! Play lip balm SPF 30

Dry air on planes can quickly dry out your lips — hydration is key. I love that the Supergoop lip balm moisturizes without feeling sticky, plus it doubles as sun protection.

Buy: Supergoop! Play Lip Balm SPF 30, $9.60 (normally $12)

How to stack rewards when online shopping

Maximize your purchases by stacking rewards through online shopping portals on top of any rewards you earn directly through your credit card. I’m a big fan of earning Amex points through Rakuten or Rove miles through Rove (they also have some of the highest earning rates I’ve seen!).

As we head into holiday shopping, keep an eye on the shopping portals for extra bonus-earning rates. Right now, you can earn up to 7 Rove miles per dollar spent at Best Buy. They also recently added personalized shopping offers with earning rates up to 25 Rove miles per dollar. If you aren’t a Rove member yet, you can join for free and earn 1,500 Rove miles instantly when you sign up using my link (that’s three times more than the standard referral offer!).

TPG tip: Multipliers change often, so check which portal offers the highest rewards via an aggregator like Cashback Monitor to maximize your rewards on all your holiday shopping this season.
